title: Purification of GFP-tagged nuclei from frozen livers of INTACT mice for RNA- and ATAC-sequencing
protocol: Sacrifice the mouse humanely following an approved ethical protocol.
Pin down the mouse and open the abdominal cavity.
Isolate all liver lobes using scissors and forceps.
Cut the liver lobes into smaller pieces (approx. 5×5 mm).
Wash liver pieces in 1× PBS.
Snap-freeze liver pieces in liquid nitrogen.
Unscrew the lid of the grinding jar and pre-chill the jar, lid, and the grinding ball in liquid nitrogen.
Put the grinding ball back into the jar, add the liver pieces into the jar and close the lid firmly.
Grind the liver tissue at 30 Hz for 1 min until completely pulverized.
Carefully transfer the pulverized tissue into a 15 mL conical tube.
Scrape off remaining pulverized tissue remnants from the side of the jar and from the grinding ball.
Precool centrifuges to 4°C.
Resuspend ∼0.5 g pulverized tissue in 4 mL ice-cold 1× PBS by tapping, e.g., in a 5 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge liver homogenate at 2,000×g for 3 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend pellet in 4 mL LSB.
Transfer to douncer and dounce 10 times with loose pestle.
Add 300 μL of a 5% IGEPAL solution to make the solution ∼0.35% IGEPAL, mix tubes and let stand at 4°C for 3–5 min.
Dounce 5 times more with tight pestle.
Filter the homogenate through a 100 μm CellTrics filter unit on a 15 mL canonical tube.
Wash the douncer with 1 mL LSB and add through the filter to homogenate in step h.
Spin filtered homogenate at 600×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend pellet in 9× volume of HSB.
Mix by pipetting.
Aliquot up to 1.8 mL in 2 mL tubes.
Double check that the nuclei pellets have gone completely into suspension before spinning again if necessary.
Spin the mixture for 15 minutes at 15,000×g at 4°C.
Remove as much supernatant as possible carefully.
Resuspend the pellets in a total of 1 mL WB, including RNasin per sample.
Pipette extensively but carefully to ensure complete resuspension after pelleting the nuclei in HSB.
Transfer first 500 μL of the resuspended mixture to a new tube.
Add an additional 500 μL WB, including RNasin, to the transferred volume.
Carry out all steps on ice or in a cold room at 4°C.
Take out 10 μL aliquot.
Dilute the aliquot 1:20 in WB.
Mix the diluted solution 1:1 with Trypan blue.
Inspect and count the nuclei under a brightfield microscope using a 10–20× objective.
Dilute the nuclei suspension to 10 mill nuclei per mL in WB, including RNasin.
Collect 15 mill nuclei (1.5 mL) for IP of hepatocyte nuclei.
Optionally collect 1 mill nuclei for whole liver nuclei RNA-seq and 25,000 for whole liver nuclei ATAC-seq.
Store the collected samples on ice until further processing.
Wash Dynabeads twice with 800 μL Wash Buffer in a 2 mL tube on a DynaMag™-2 Magnet.
Batch-wash Protein G Dynabeads in 15 mL tubes using a DynaMag™-15 magnet.
Use 1350 μL beads and 12 mL WB for enough beads for 12 nuclear preparations.
Resuspend beads in 100 μL per sample of WB, including RNasin.
Pipette 20 μL of beads into new 2 mL tube labeled “Preclear”.
Transfer nuclei suspension into the preclear tube and mix.
End-to-end rotate at 4°C for 10–15 min.
Prepare 2 mL tubes with 3 μg of anti-GFP antibody and 200 μL WB, including RNasin in each tube.
Place precleared sample on magnet for 4-5 min.
While standing on the magnet, pipette supernatant from the precleared sample into the tube with antibody.
End-to-end rotate at 4°C for 30 min.
Resuspend remaining 80 μL of washed beads and add to tube with antibody and nuclei.
End-to-end rotate at 4°C for 20 min.
Place sample on magnet for 4-5 min.
While standing on the magnet, completely remove supernatant.
Add 1.8 mL of WB and let sit for 30 seconds.
Pipette extensively up and down to resuspend.
Pipette up and down an additional 5 times after initial resuspension.
Repeat the pipetting steps twice more.
Place the tube on a magnet, add 1 mL WB including RNasin, and let sit over nuclei for 2 minutes before resuspending.
Take out a 10 μL aliquot of bead-bound nuclei.
Dilute the aliquot 1:5 in WB.
Mix diluted sample 1:1 with Trypan blue.
Count the number of nuclei using a brightfield microscope at a 10–20× objective.
Calculate the fraction of recovered nuclei by comparing to whole liver nuclei initially added.
Add 1 μL DAPI to a 10 μL aliquot of bead-bound and whole liver nuclei (diluted to approximately 7500 nuclei/μL).
Count 100–200 nuclei with a fluorescence microscope equipped with appropriate filters for detecting GFP and DAPI using a 10–20× objective.
Quantify the number of bead-bound GFP+ nuclei vs. DAPI-stained nuclei in both samples.
Determine the purity by considering the fraction of GFP+ nuclei vs total DAPI-stained nuclei in the bead-bound sample.
Calculate the expected number of recovered GFP+ nuclei using the formula: Expected # of GFP+ nuclei = Total # of nuclei added to IP x % GFP+ nuclei in the original whole liver sample.
Compare the actual number of recovered GFP+ nuclei with the expected number.
Harvest nuclei for RNA isolation.
Spin down 1 mill nuclei at 600×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and leave 20–30 μL WB, incl. RNasin behind to resuspend pellet again.
Vortex nuclei to resuspend, add 500 μL of TRIzol and vortex until nuclei are completely dissolved.
Use a magnet to remove supernatant leaving 20–30 μL WB, incl. RNasin behind to resuspend pellet again.
Briefly spin down to collect nuclei and WB in the bottom of the tube.
Vortex, immediately add 500 μL of TRIzol and vortex until completely dissolved.
Add 0.2 volume (100 μL) of chloroform.
Vortex vigorously for 30 seconds to mix phases.
Incubate 15 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Spin at 10,000×g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the upper phase (approximately 200 μL) to a 1.5 mL tube and place on ice.
Add 0.6 volume (120 μL) of 96% ethanol.
Briefly vortex and briefly spin down.
Load the indicated volume onto an EconoSpin microcolumn.
Spin at 13,000×g for 30 seconds at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the column once with 500 μL diluted RPE buffer at 20°C–25°C.
Spin at 13,000×g for 30 seconds at 20°C–25°C and discard the flow-through.
Make a DNase I mix by combining 10 μL of DNase I stock solution with 70 μL Buffer RDD.
Mix gently by inverting the tube and spin down before use.
Add the DNase I mix (80 μL) directly to the microcolumn membrane.
Place on the benchtop (20°C–30°C) for 15 minutes.
Add 500 μL diluted RPE buffer to the microcolumn with the DNase I incubation mix.
Close the lid gently and centrifuge at 13,000×g for 30 seconds at 20°C–25°C to wash the spin column membrane free of DNase I.
Discard the flow-through and collection tube.
Place the microcolumn in a new 2 mL collection tube.
Wash the microcolumn one additional time with 500 μL diluted RPE buffer.
Spin at 13,000×g for 30 seconds at 20°C–25°C and discard the flow through.
Place the microcolumn back in a new collection tube.
Spin dry the column at 13,000×g for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Transfer the column to a fresh 1.5 mL tube carefully without touching the sides of the microcolumn.
Incubate the column with the lid open for 5–10 minutes at 20°C–25°C to completely evaporate residual ethanol.
Elute in 16 μL RNAse-free water by adding it to the center of the column.
Incubate for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C after elution.
Spin at 9,000×g for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C and collect the eluate.
Measure the RNA concentration and quality on 1 μL of sample using a Nanodrop.
Determine RNA integrity optionally.
Measure the quality of the RNA using Bioanalyzer profiles.
Manually inspect the RNA integrity based on the Bioanalyzer profiles.
Compare the amount of degraded RNA in buffers with and without RNasin.
Observe that adding RNasin to the buffers reduces RNA degradation.
Note the absence of peaks corresponding to 18S and 28S rRNA fragments for nuclear RNA.
Prepare RNA for sequencing using the VAHTS Stranded mRNA-seq Library Kit for Illumina according to the manufacturer’s recommendations.
Add 5 μL of diluted RNA directly to 13.5 μL of Frag/Prime Buffer to fragment the RNA before proceeding with cDNA synthesis.
Thaw 5× TTBL from the TruePrep DNA Library Prep Kit V2 at 20°C–25°C by inverting.
Spin down 25,000 nuclei at 600×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant completely using a magnet.
Take a volume corresponding to 25,000 nuclei.
Prepare a transposition reaction mastermix (50 μL per sample).
Resuspend the nuclear pellet directly in the transposition reaction mixture by gently pipetting for 20 times.
Place the tube in the thermal block at 37°C for 30 minutes at 1000×rpm with heat lid on at 105°C.
Add 5 volumes (250 μL) of Buffer ERC and 5 μL Na-acetate (3 M, pH = 5.2) to the transposition reaction mix.
Mix by vortexing and incubate for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Transfer the cleaned-up reaction mix by placing mixture on the magnet and transferring supernatant to a MinElute column for bead-bound nuclei.
Proceed with Qiagen MinElute Reaction Cleanup according to manufacturers' recommendations.
Elute DNA in 21 μL elution buffer.
Perform cleanup of libraries after the PCR using MinElute PCR Purification Kit according to the manufacturer’s recommendations.
Elute in 21 μL elution buffer.
Run 1 μL of each library (diluted 1:3 in water) using the High Sensitivity DNA kit.
Fill up the volume to a total 50 μl with nuclease-free water before the next step.
Mix AMPure® XP beads by vortexing and add 32.5 μL (0.65×) of beads to the purified PCR products (50 μL).
Mix thoroughly by gently pipetting for 10 times.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 5 min.
Place the reaction tube on the magnetic stand after brief centrifugation.
Let the tube rest until the solution completely clarifies (around 5 min).
Transfer the supernatant carefully to a new tube and discard the beads.
Mix AMPure® XP beads by vortexing.
Add 55 μL of beads to the supernatant.
Mix thoroughly by gently pipetting for 10 times.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 5 min.
Place the reaction tube on the magnetic stand after brief centrifugation.
Let the tube rest until the solution completely clarifies.
Remove the supernatant carefully and store the beads.
Add 200 μL of fresh prepared 80% ethanol to wash the beads.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 30 s and discard the supernatant.
Repeat for a total of two washes.
Open the tube lid and air-dry the beads at 20°C–25°C for 5 min.
Remove the tube from magnetic stand and add 20 μL of nuclease-free water to elute the DNA.
Mix by vortexing or gently pipetting.
Place the reaction tube in the magnetic frame after brief centrifugation.
Let the tube rest until the solution completely clarifies.
Carefully remove 18 μL of supernatant to a new tube.
Spin down 2 mill nuclei at 600×g for 5 minutes (whole liver nuclei) or use a magnet (bead-bound nuclei).
Completely remove all the supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 20 μL WB.
Add an equal volume of 20 μL NUN extraction buffer and pipet extensively up and down.
Vortex, spin down shortly after 3–4 rounds of pipetting when solution starts to clump.
Incubate on ice for 20 minutes.
Spin 10 minutes at 21,000×g at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant to a new tube.
Take a small aliquot out for determination of the protein concentration.
Determine nuclear protein concentration using e.g., the BCA Protein Assay Kit according to the manufacturer’s recommendations.
